title: Hotline contingency scratch (jamal)
content:
Purpose: quick personal prep + live-notes for a daytime hotline war-room with AcmeCorp (billing spike + token errors).

Top objectives (quick):
- Triage scope: confirm is this: model timeout vs. token rejection vs. downstream DB errors?
- Stabilize customer experience: apply short-term mitigation (throttle, fallback model, cache responses)
- Communication: one clear timeline and owner for customer updates (15m cadence)
- Post-mortem seeds: capture root-cause evidence and key metrics for follow-up

Initial facts (from support thread / logs):
- Customer: AcmeCorp (tenant acme-prod) reported high error rate 10:45 PST.
- Symptoms: 500s for generate endpoint; some 429s for embeddings (burst).
- Recent change: they started a batch job at 10:30 that increased concurrent requests to routing-service.
- Observed in metrics: spike in latency on us-west-2 serving pool; GC churn on model-node-7; kernel OOMs on gpu-pool-b at 10:41.

Immediate owners / roles (who to ping):
- Customer comms (owner): Jamal Carter -> post updates, coordinate expectations
- Eng on-call (first): Maya Chen -> check serving runtime, revert recent routing weight changes
- SRE (infra): Ravi Singh -> check GPU host health, node restarts, autoscale triggers
- DB / downstream: Sofia Alvarez -> confirm DB request queue, rate limiter events
- Solutions eng (backup): Priya Rao (if we need a tailored customer workaround)

Quick checklist (first 15m):
1) Confirm incident channel open: #cust-escalation-hotline (I opened at 10:55).
2) Snapshot top logs: gather last 30m from serving-runtime logs and gpu metrics (Maya)
3) Pause non-essential background jobs from AcmeCorp (they agreed to pause batch at 11:00).
4) Apply temporary throughput cap at routing layer for acme-prod (Ravi) -> reduce bursts, relieve gpu-pool-b
5) If 500s persist, fallback to smaller model (gpt-small-v2) for critical routes (Maya + Jamal to decide)
6) If kernel OOMs continue, spin up additional nodes (Ravi) or move traffic to us-east-1 as contingency

Communication template (15m cadence):
- 00:15 update: what we know, who is working it, next check-in time
- 00:30 update: any mitigations applied + immediate effect metrics (error rate, latency p95)
- Holding message if no new info: "Investigating with infra + runtime; next update in 15 minutes"

Key technical investigation threads to capture:
- Routing config changes (recent deploys) -> link to PR or config id (look for PR/commit)
- Kernel OOM traces -> nv-crash logs, dmesg, container OOM killers
- KV cache behavior -> cache miss storm? prefix mismatch? (could explain extra compute)
- Autoscale trigger logs -> did autoscaler delay because of quotas?

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Batch job created a sudden spike -> concurrency exhaustion + KV cache miss storm -> GC + kernel OOMs -> 500s
2) Recent routing weight change sent too much to gpu-pool-b which has a failing node -> OOM cascade
3) Model variant degradation (quantization regression) causing memory blowups (less likely but check recent model release)

Notes-to-self / gotchas:
- Keep track of token accounting when switching models (cost implications for customer)
- If we failover to east, check routing latency impact and whether customer allows cross-region data flow
- Watch for noisy metrics: p50 might hide tail; use p95/p99

Temporary mitigation decision matrix (quick):
- If error_rate > 10% and p95 latency > 3s: throttle non-critical routes + fallback to small model for chat-likely flows
- If OOMs present on node(s): cordon node, drain, rebuild; move traffic away immediately

Live notes (to fill during call):
- 10:55 JAM: opened channel, asked for sample request ids -> support gave rids: rid-3345, rid-3347
- 11:02 MAYA: discovered GC spikes on model-node-7 at 10:41; kernel logs show oom_killer activity
- 11:08 RAVI: autoscale didn't add nodes due to quota limit (quota-gpu-20 reached) -> opened cloud request
- 11:12 SOFIA: DB queue normal; no downstream errors found
- 11:18 JAM: asked customer to pause batch job, they confirmed pause at 11:20

Decisions made (stamped):
- 11:22 -> throttle acme-prod to 60% of previous throughput (Ravi applied routing cap)
- 11:25 -> fallback for critical generate route to gpt-small-v2, applied via canary (Maya)
- 11:30 -> requested temporary GPU quota bump from cloud provider, ETA 40m (Ravi)

Post-meeting action items (owners + due):
- Jamal: send external incident summary to AcmeCorp and confirm acceptable mitigation (due EOD today)
- Maya: open an ops-issue for GC tuning and memory profiling on model-node-7 (due 2026-03-15)
- Ravi: follow up with cloud account team for quota bump and permanent capacity plan (due 2026-03-18)
- Sofia: validate that DB is not the root cause and document correlation metrics (due 2026-03-14)
- Priya: draft customer-facing rollback plan for any config changes (due 2026-03-16)

Evidence to collect for post-mortem:
- Serving runtime logs (10:00-12:00) filtered by acme-prod tenant
- Node-level metrics (GPU memory, CPU, dmesg) for gpu-pool-b nodes
- Autoscaler event history and quota error messages
- Routing config snapshots / commit history for last 24h
- Sample failed requests and full request/response traces for rid-3345/3347

Open questions (to surface in PM):
- Is our autoscaler configured with conservative cooldowns that delay scale-up?
- Should we add a soft throttle policy per-tenant to avoid noisy neighbors in the future?
- Can we improve early-warning for KV cache miss storms (heatmap + alert)?

Post-mortem seeds (ideas):
- Add per-tenant burst protection: token buckets / leaky-bucket at routing layer
- Runbook tweak: explicitly check GPU quotas before applying routing weight changes that increase concurrency
- Observability: alert on kernel OOM trends + correlate with p99 latency spikes

Personal notes / scribbles (messy):
- customer is reasonable; avoid scaring them with "OOM" in external comms -> phrase as "resource pressure on serving nodes"
- remind PM to follow up on SLA credit asks after root cause confirmed
- probably need a short 30m retro with eng+sre next week to finalize capacity plan

Finish: keep this doc as live log during the hotline until stabilized. After incident wrap, move key lines to confluence incident doc and file JIRA for follow-ups.

-- Jamal (notes)
